methodology: The BareBoard Top 100 lists DEVICES — finished products end users use, like an Amazon Echo or a Ring doorbell. Chips, dev boards, and components (ESP32, STM32 boards, Raspberry Pi boards, Arduino) are not devices and are excluded. Ranking is by real-world use in 2026: active installed base and devices still in use today first, lifetime units sold second, from published figures only (company disclosures, official console sales, analyst reporting). Fact-checked 2026-10-15. Where no model-level figure is published, placement rests on category scale, distribution channel, production model, and longevity, and the entry's usage_evidence field says so — no figure is invented. Removed entries (the non-devices plus the bottom of the list by use) are preserved in Dropbox (/BareBoard-Site-Archive/hot-150-removed-bottom-50.json); the full previous Hot 150 (v2.0) is kept as hot150-original-v2.json.
ranking_basis: Devices only (finished end-user products), ranked by real-world use in 2026 (installed base / units in use), from published figures.

evidence_labels.confirmed: Multiple corroborating sources, including a published teardown.
evidence_labels.likely: At least one solid verifiable source (reference article or official product page).
evidence_labels.unconfirmed: Limited sourcing; official page unverified or thin corroboration.

selection_criteria: Device must have genuine hardware-hacker relevance (teardown interest, chip curiosity, repairability, or modding scene).
Device must have at least one verifiable public source URL.
No invented specifications, sales figures, or rankings.
Preference for devices with published teardowns or open hardware documentation.
Categories cover phones, SBCs, consoles, laptops, IoT, drones, VR, wearables, audio, tablets, networking, and hacker tools.

repair_guide_policy: A repair guide is the device's iFixit page (device page, teardown, or repair guide) or the manufacturer's official repair/service/support documentation. Not YouTube, not blogs, not review sites. Every link verified live (HTTP 200, correct device AND model) before shipping. Where neither exists, the card says so honestly. Per the owner's link rule, the site links to preserved copies in archive.org/bareboardorg — fill archive_url after saving page copies (Dropbox /BareBoard-Site-Archive/).
